From questions to clean events

The first hour can shed demo detail. The hands-on hour keeps its full 60 minutes. Open each slide title to jump the deck to that point.

Open slides Workshop hub

Pre-flight

  • Open the prepared Amplitude project, funnel, replay, Journeys chart, cohort, Braze segment, guide, and experiment.
  • Test project creation permissions in the attendee account.
  • Load the app through the venue network and send one event to a throwaway project.
  • Keep the slides, talk track, app, and Amplitude in separate tabs.
  • Have an offline copy of the pack. The app still demonstrates payloads if Amplitude is unavailable.
  • Send the pre-work on the hub the day before, and bring a standby project API key for anyone blocked at Station 3.
  • If you want the room to see Web Experiment working, bring a client-side deployment key with a running web experiment on it. Without one the field stays empty and Station 3 is unaffected.
  • Have every demo tab open and logged in before the room fills. Five surfaces in 34 minutes leaves no room for a cold start.

Hard gate at 0:38. Move to the data model whatever is unfinished in the speed run. Each demo carries a CUT line; use it. The hands-on hour does not absorb demo overrun, and Station 5 is the only buffer left after that. If the room is already behind at 0:22, the Braze block is the one to cut to a screenshot walk — it depends on a configured destination and is the least actionable step for this audience.

Answer key: what's wrong with the shipped plan

Don't hand this out and don't walk the room through it. Use it to ask the question that gets a stuck table unstuck, and to confirm a catch when somebody finds one.

ActionAs shippedProblemsShould be
Adds a taskclicked_add_button
  • Named after the button that was clicked, not the action the person completed.
  • snake_case here, Title Case elsewhere, camelCase on delete. Pick one.
  • list_size is sent as a string, so it can't be averaged or bucketed.
  • role and analytics_experience describe the person, not this occurrence. They belong on the user.
  • entry_method is missing, so the second half of the question has no answer.

  • Shares one name with reopening, so nothing distinguishes finishing work from undoing it.
  • age_seconds is missing, so 'how long does completion take' has no answer.

task_position: number
age_seconds: number

  • Collapsed into the same event as completion.
  • age_seconds is missing.

task_id: string
age_seconds: number
list_size: number
Deletes a tasktaskDeleted
  • camelCase, unlike every other event here.
  • was_completed arrives as the string 'yes' or 'no', so it can't be filtered as a boolean.
  • client_timestamp duplicates the event time Amplitude already records.
Task Deleted
task_id: string
was_completed: boolean
age_seconds: number
list_size: number
Changes the list filterFilter Changed - {filter}
  • The filter value is baked into the event name, so the taxonomy grows one event per filter.
  • filter isn't a property, so you can't group one event by the view somebody chose.
List Filter Changed
filter: string
visible_task_count: number
Opens somebody else's shared listOpen Shared List
  • Action then object, while every other event here is object then action.
Shared List Opened

User properties

  • last_task_id and last_filter describe the latest action, not the person. They overwrite on every identify.
  • workshop_table is missing, so you can't group the room by table.

Already correct: edits a task (Task Edited) and copies a share link (List Shared). Leaving these alone is part of the exercise — if a table "fixes" everything, ask them what was wrong with these two.

The one to make sure the room sees: the filter event bakes its value into the name, so Amplitude fills up with Filter Changed - all, Filter Changed - active, and Filter Changed - completed instead of one event you can group. It's the most visible mistake in Station 4 and the most common one in real taxonomies.

Welcome and route

From questions to clean events

Welcome the room. The first hour follows one analysis from a funnel into qualitative evidence, paths, activation, and an experiment. The second hour starts with a finished app. Attendees make the measurement decisions and then watch their events arrive in Amplitude.

Two hours, two modes

0:38–0:53
teach · 15 min

The Amplitude data model

What arrives in Amplitude

Move from consuming data to producing it. Every chart in the speed run depended on event order, event context, and identity. The exercise starts from user behavior and works forward into that model.

Three parts of the tracking plan

Use one concrete example. Event names describe completed actions. Event properties belong to one occurrence. User properties describe the person and remain available on later events until changed.

Identity changes the analysis

Drive the panel live. Add two anonymous events, then sign in and add a third: the device's earlier activity resolves to the person, which is why the Braze cohort in the first hour had somebody to match. Then untick Set a user ID and add more events to show sign-in becoming invisible to analytics. IDs need at least five characters under the SDK default. Don't use an email address for this exercise.

1:07–1:19
hands-on · 12 min

Station 1: Audit the event names

Audit the event names

Give pairs 12 minutes. Ask them to write their own names first: once they've read the shipped plan they'll anchor to it. Two of the eight are already correct, so listen for tables that are 'fixing' everything. Ask what decision each event supports and what the name would look like in a chart. At minute 75, tell the room they have four minutes left.

The user actions

Leave this slide up while pairs work. All eight actions are also in the guide. They don't have to instrument every action; choosing not to track something is part of the plan.

Room done when: The app's event names match a plan you would defend, and anything you chose not to track is unticked.

1:19–1:31
hands-on · 12 min

Station 2: Fix the properties

Fix the properties

Give pairs 12 minutes. Every property chip can be ticked, unticked, and in two places retyped, so this is a real repair rather than a paper one. Push on the two questions that matter: does a chart need this, and does it describe the person or this one occurrence? A string that holds a number is the type mistake most people walk past.

Check each property

Use these checks when the room asks what belongs in the plan. More properties don't automatically make better data.

Room done when: Each event carries the context its question needs and nothing it can't justify, and person context sits on the user rather than on every event.

1:31–1:39
hands-on · 8 min

Station 3: Connect Amplitude

Connect Amplitude

Demo the project settings path in the room's Amplitude account, then let attendees work. The app uses the Browser SDK and disables automatic tracking so every workshop event is intentional. Pair anyone blocked by permissions.

Connection details

Keep this visible during connection. The API key is a public client-side identifier, and the whole app state sits in the URL: key, tracking plan, profile, and list. Copying the address bar carries the lot to another browser or device, which is how somebody picks up where they left off or hands their setup to a partner. Anyone with the link can send events to that project, so it belongs in a DM rather than a public channel.

Replay and experiments ride along

Point at the Wire entries in the Activity panel. Session Replay is a plugin added before init, and it works by stamping a replay ID onto each event, which is the same join we used in the first hour to get from the funnel to a recording. The app masks every text node, so replays show what somebody did without what they typed: decide that before you ship replay, not after. The Web Experiment field is optional and needs a client-side deployment key with a running experiment, so most tables will leave it empty.

Room done when: The app shows Connected and the Activity panel records an Identify call.

1:39–1:51
hands-on · 12 min

Station 4: Generate and verify events

Generate and verify events

Allow 12 minutes. Events may take a short time to appear. Have attendees search for their generated user ID. If an event is missing, check the app response, ad blockers, project region, and API key before changing the schema.

When an event is missing

Use the sequence as a fast debugging guide. The app records both preview payloads and SDK responses. Ad blockers can block the SDK or requests. A US/EU mismatch sends data to the wrong endpoint for the project.

Room done when: At least three event types appear in Amplitude with the event and property names you planned.

1:51–1:57
optional · 6 min

Station 5: Ask one question

Ask one question

This station is the buffer. If there are fewer than six minutes left, skip the build and ask two people which chart they would make. The sample is too small for a real product conclusion; the point is testing whether the schema supports the query.

Room done when: A chart answers one question from your plan and its limitation is written down.
